speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these symptoms of double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness, and do they seem to get worse as the day goes on?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing, speaking, or shortness of breath that might indicate involvement of your throat or breathing muscles? Also, has anyone in your family been diagnosed with similar neuromuscular conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any drooping of the eyelids or facial weakness, particularly later in the day? I also need to check your reflexes, so could you sit still while I tap your knee and elbow tendons?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: I'll check your reflexes now, so please relax while I tap your knee and elbow tendons. Do you notice any drooping of your eyelids or facial weakness, especially as the day progresses?

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the pattern of fatigable weakness without muscle wasting, I will now examine your pupils and eye movements for specific signs. REQUEST IMAGES: Eye examination and pupil response. Do you notice any changes in your vision when looking straight ahead versus looking up?

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your fatigable weakness and the eye findings, I need to confirm the presence of an antibody causing this condition. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine receptor antibody. Do you have any history of thymoma or thyroid issues?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Chest_CT: Normal, no thymoma or other masses detected; Neurological_Examination: Presence of ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) that worsens with sustained upward gaze; Diminished motor strength observed in the upper extremities; Electromyography: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; Vital_Signs: Temperature 36.6°C (97.9°F), Blood_Pressure 125/80 mmHg, Heart_Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory_Rate 16 breaths/min.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results confirm the presence of acetylcholine receptor antibodies alongside fatigable weakness and ptosis, which are classic signs of Myasthenia Gravis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.
